entries.title: Two-factor authentication, request approvals, and more
notes: Sign-in can now ask for a code from an authenticator app (or a one-time backup code) as a second step -- turn it on from the account menu, under Security.
New accounts, password resets, and sign-in name changes now go to the admin for approval instead of taking effect immediately.
"Raise a request" in the topbar sends a feature idea, a bug, or a question straight to the admin, and shows you its status.
The data folder now backs itself up automatically once a day, with a manual "Back up now" and downloadable backups in the admin panel.
New passwords need at least 10 characters, and can't be the sign-in name or a common password.
Each dashboard card now shows when its data was last updated.
A new admin panel: live sessions, accounts, login history (with IP), pending requests, suggestions, backups, and per-dashboard visibility.
The admin panel's Accounts card now shows each person's designation, department, category, phone, email and Paras ID, with an "Edit profile" button to correct any of them.
Login history is now grouped per person, most recently active first, with a click to expand their full history and a "Load more" for a longer window.
A new "Usage" view per account shows time spent per day or per month, which dashboards were viewed and for how long, and whether that person is signed in right now.
Sign-up now also offers IT and Management as departments, GCOO/MD/CHRO as designations, and "All" as a category, with the designation/department/category fields shown three across instead of two.
A "How to sign in / reset your password" link on the sign-in screen opens a short walkthrough of the current sign-in, reset, sign-up and 2FA flow.

entries.title: Email: sign-up verification, admin notifications, broadcasts
notes: Once email is set up on the server (see set_mail.py), sign-up now sends a verification code to the address you type -- the request can't be sent until you enter it back.
The admin is emailed the moment a new signup, password reset, or sign-in name change lands in the pending-requests queue.
A new "Broadcast email" card in the admin panel sends a message to every account with an email on file, or to specific accounts you pick.
All of the above quietly does nothing until email is configured -- nothing about sign-up, requests, or the admin panel changes on a server that hasn't run set_mail.py.
